chapter_theme: Ramadevar's ten-stanza rule of worship (பூஜாவிதி), attributed. It opens as a Shakta instruction: know the primal lamp, see the boundless fullness, hold the root, the maiden and the three letters in the central breath, and recite the three letters a lakh of times for siddhi. It then turns to a rite against an enemy, with offering, cremation ash, a figure, a stake driven under a tree and recitations of a hundred and eight, and closes by naming the auspicious days and promising that the ten verses yield siddhi and release.
structure_note: 1530 to 1533 are doctrine and the mantra: the lamp of the beginning, the fullness, the maiden at the root, the triangle and the three letters. 1534 to 1537 describe the killing rite step by step and its result. 1538 fixes the days and names the powers. 1539 is the colophon, naming Rama and the ten verses.

1530.reading: One must know the gem-lamp called the beginning, see the boundless fullness; all the paths of the pure space called light, for the sake of bliss, are our Mother Manonmani; the feet of the supreme light called justice, the state in which she stands without qualities, none see; standing within the Vedanta called the Veda, this puja will not go in vain.
1530.nuance: The chapter's goddess is Manonmani, the Mother; the puja is to her as the formless fullness, and the verse says the formless state is unseen even while promising the puja a result. The Vedanta is invoked as the ground of a tantric rite.

1531.reading: You who stand without going: having gained the five kalas of fullness and the creeper of bliss that does not become, in the breath between foot and crown within the six, by the root that bears the maiden, one must utter the three letters by which the way appears; this root dies without dying; the moon-circle, the middle angle, is the triangle.
1531.nuance: அடிமுடி நடுவாசி ஆறுக்குள்ளே is read as the breath held in the central channel through the six centres. The maiden (வாலை) at the root is the young goddess as the body's power; the three letters are taken by tradition as அ உ ம or as the goddess's seed syllables. சசிவட்டம், the moon's circle, and the triangle are the yantra of the next verse. The grammar is loose and the reading is approximate.

1532.reading: The triangle becomes the three whorls and the self-angle, and in the maiden, the first root-gem, the four lines of the square are to be guarded with care; when the Lady, the supreme light, has fixed her gaze, I have told in detail the delusion that stood in the direction of the fire-angle, to be understood; if the lack of the fire-angle has come, the one who sat alone and saw is the siddha.
1532.nuance: The verse describes a drawn chakra, a triangle within a square with a corner of fire (தீக்கோணம், the south-east), while hinting at the body's three channels (மூசுழி). தாக்கோண விட்டகுறை is obscure, perhaps a defect left in the fire-corner; the siddha is the one who has sat alone and seen for himself.

1533.reading: The three letters that became siddhi are the light that acts; they become the fine aim, kilee and sav; to recite them a lakh of times is to complete siddhi even against the ghosts called enemies; this is the seed-knowledge, see where it strikes; hear the three wide face-seeds, and setting their strong seed in the figure, hear in detail the fourfold rule.
1533.nuance: ஐயும் கிலியும் சவ்வும் are the goddess's seed syllables aim, klim and sauh, here as the three letters of 1531, so the earlier reading as அ உ ம is not the only one. The verse turns the mantra toward enemies and introduces the figure (சிலை) into which the seed is set, which the following verses use.

1534.reading: Listen: having given an offering and done the puja, having fixed the form with the gracious recitation, bury it well in the ash of the burning ground at midnight; then, cut at the root, he becomes death, the state of austerity he held is ruined, and, dear one, the sinner will fall; I tell you so the story is understood, see further.
1534.nuance: This is a rite of destruction (மாரணம் in the tantras, though the word is not used): a charged figure buried in cremation ash to bring an enemy's death and the collapse of his tapas. The verse claims it works; the poem offers it as the dark side of the same mantra. It is recorded here as the text's claim, not as anything to be done.

1535.reading: There will be still further tests before the eyes; if you want to be saved, the secret is in this: make a peg of agil wood or devadaru with knowledge, utter the lion-syllable, say the name of the one meant and 'perish', cast the hundred and eight strong forms, and sitting under the tree drive the peg in skilfully with a nail.
1535.nuance: சூட்சம், the secret, is the Siddhars' word for the hidden point of a practice, here applied to a nailing rite. The hundred and eight is the standard count of recitation. Several phrases, அன்னமின்னா, சன்னமின்னா, are filler or corrupt and leave the wood and the place uncertain.

1536.reading: Pull out the peg you drove and set it bound tight; the form of bliss will be broken and perish; from the day begun, on the fourth day, you yourself will see the count finished and the way of this ... come to be; after release the poison rises and the instrument departs; I have told it fully, this is the bolt, it will not go in vain; stop it, strike it in the city and see, the frame is wrecked and life is lost as harm.
1536.nuance: The verse states the rite's effect, death on the fourth day, and calls the teaching a பூட்டு, a bolt or lock, the Siddhars' term for a secret meant to be hard to open. உயிர்புதலாய் is probably corrupt. The reading is a paraphrase of a damaged text.

1537.reading: Yes, if it is at the foot-vision in the arena, see, those who see it will take refuge in wonder; I have spoken opening the space, see, this way is no game; bathe with purity, head and all, and meditate quickly on the Mother's root; I have spoken the truth, see, this is Rama's word, without fail.
1537.nuance: The verse steps back from the rite to its frame: ritual bathing, meditation on the Mother's root mantra, and the author's oath. அடிதரிசிங் களத்தில் is obscure; perhaps the vision at the feet in the ritual ground. ராமனுடை வாக்யம் names Ramadevar as the speaker.

1538.reading: Perform siddhi with the root called 'I'; siddhi lies within the hundred and eight; the eight seats of the gods will dance, all the sixty-four herbs will dance, the trumpeted siddhis will dance in an instant; it is good to do it on the day of Revati, good on the eighth lunar day, and the one who does it in the waxing moon is a yogi.
1538.nuance: தானென்ற மூலம், the root mantra called 'I' or 'that', is left unexplained. The powers promised are the eight siddhis (அண்டர் பதி எட்டு) and command over the sixty-four herbs of the medical siddhas. The timing by star, tithi and fortnight is the astrological frame the Siddhars share with the Tirumanthiram's breath-calendar.

1539.reading: I told you this for becoming a yogi; oho, by the root taught before, as yogis, under the Lady of solitude, since it was written on the leaf all is done; by the grace of the thirsty Mother it becomes austerity, becomes ... , brings good; by the ten rules of root-puja for the infatuated, siddhi ripens for release: the ten are complete.
1539.nuance: The colophon counts the ten verses and claims both siddhi and முத்தி from them. தவமாகும் மவமாகும் is a jingle whose second word is unclear, perhaps 'and un-austerity', that is, good and ill alike. ஏகாந்த வல்லி, the Lady of solitude, is the goddess as the yogi's sole companion.

links.note: Both place the practice in the central channel between root and crown: Tirumular's sushumna running under the rising fire with sun and moon on their way, Ramadevar's breath between foot and crown within the six, at the root that bears the maiden.

Three letters that bring the light: Tirumular says by three letters the light springs up, Ramadevar that the way appears by uttering the three letters at the root. Which three letters is not fixed in either text.

Both set the maiden at the root as the power to be met: Tirumular's transmuting maiden who rouses the form rising from the root region, Ramadevar's first root-gem who is the maiden within the triangle.

Both texts turn mantra and drawn figure to a magical end and promise a visible result: Tirumular's palm-leaf figure smeared with wax and warmed for stambhana, Ramadevar's seed set in a figure and recited a lakh of times against enemies. The Tirumanthiram's chakra tantra is the precedent for the Siddhar rite.

The Kural says not killing is the whole of virtue and that killing brings every other evil; Ramadevar's rite is a procedure meant to bring an enemy's death and calls its teaching a secret for being saved. On any reading of 1534 as a killing rite, the two are incompatible.

Both set a practice by the calendar: Tirumular's breath runs left or right by the weekday and the fortnight, Ramadevar's rite is good on Revati, on the eighth day and in the waxing moon. The timing is shared; what is timed, breath against rite, differs.

Both name Manonmani: for Tirumular she is one of the names by which the great goddess stands as many; for Ramadevar she is the Mother who is all the paths of the pure space, the formless fullness the puja addresses.

source_issues: The whole work carries the attribution 'attributed'; 1537 names Rama as the speaker from within the text.
1535 and 1536 have several unparsable phrases (அன்னமின்னா, வன்னமின்னார், சன்னமின்னா, உயிர்புதலாய்); the ritual text is damaged and the readings are approximate.
1532 line 7 தாக்கோண விட்டகுறை and 1537 line 1 அடிதரிசிங் களத்தில் are obscure, possibly corrupt.
1534 to 1537 describe a rite meant to kill; marked here for what the text claims, not restated as a procedure.
